$comment: Charles HTTP debugging proxy 4.6.7 TLS fingerprint — older Charles release (~2019) running on Java 8 SSLEngine. Differs from charles_5_1.json in two Java 8-era specifics: (1) tls_min_version is tls11 because Java 8 still negotiated TLS 1.0/1.1 by default, and (2) session_id_length is 32 because the JDK 8 SSLEngine sent a 32-byte legacy_session_id placeholder on every ClientHello (later Java 11+ stopped doing this on fresh connections, which is why Charles 5.1 captures show session_id_length=0). Cipher list, signature algorithms, and the fixed raw payloads of ext 50 (signature_algorithms_cert) and ext 17 (status_request_v2) are identical to 5.1. SNI (ext 0) was missing from the original capture (capture tool stripped it for privacy) but is added at position 0 because Java SSLEngine has always emitted SNI first; without it any virtual-hosted origin silently drops the ClientHello. Not byte-verified against a real Charles 4.6.7 capture — derived from a fingerprint export shared by the user. For byte-verified accuracy use charles_5_1.json instead.
name: Charles 4.6.7

extensions._comment: server_name (SNI) — Java SSLEngine always emits SNI first; original capture stripped it for privacy
signature_algorithms_cert (Java explicitly emits this; payload is the same 19-entry list as ext 13, length 0x0026 = 38 bytes)
status_request_v2 (Java/JDK only; list len 7, OCSP-MULTI type 2, responder_id_list/extensions all empty)
supported_versions (Java still sends this even when capped at TLS 1.2; auto-generated from tls_min/max_version)
